questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to fix a computer that keeps freezing up
A new subject studying how people and the web interact
The history of big companies like Microsoft and Apple
Why online adverts have become so annoying lately
questions.why: They hear about Web Science and ask if it could make the internet better for humanity.

questions.q: Why is Neil upset at the start?
options: A video he was watching wouldn't stop buffering
He saw some hateful comments about himself online
He couldn't find a website he needed for work
His computer froze and he lost an hour's work
questions.why: He says his computer suddenly froze and he lost everything.

questions.q: What problem with the internet does Sam mention?
options: It can spread hate and misinformation
It is too expensive for most people
It is getting slower every year
It is only available in big cities
questions.why: Sam says the internet also provides a way of spreading hate and misinformation.

questions.q: What was the theme of this year's Web Science conference?
options: Making computers faster
Stopping cyber crime
Making the web focused on humans
Teaching children to code
questions.why: Neil says its theme was 'making the web human-centric'.

questions.q: According to Dame Wendy Hall, how do most people misunderstand the web?
options: They think it was invented quite recently, in the 2000s
They see it as just technology, not made by society
They think it is secretly controlled by one company
They believe it is powered entirely by AI these days
questions.why: She says people think of the web as a technology, but actually it's co-created by society.

questions.q: Which subjects does Web Science combine with digital technology?
options: Only computer science, statistics and maths
History, geography and modern languages
Medicine, law and environmental studies
Psychology, robotics, economics and sociology
questions.why: Neil says it combines technology with subjects from psychology and robotics to economics and sociology.

questions.q: What doubt does Carly Kind have about Covid contact tracing apps?
options: Most people simply won't bother to download them
They use far too much battery on older phones
Bluetooth may not be good enough to detect contact
They collect and share too much personal data
questions.why: She questions whether Bluetooth is adequate and says the trials show it's not that great.

questions.q: Why does Sam mention the Covid app as an example?
options: To show how websites can help people in useful ways
To show that apps like this are always useless
To explain how the web was first invented in the 1980s
To advertise the app to listeners and ask them to use it
questions.why: Sam calls the contact tracing app an example of websites helpfully interacting with humans.
